recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Do not reopen FHIR-7660 to reintroduce dischargeDiagnosis; route any remaining diagnosis-use value set concern through FHIR-50827 or a new final PA/terminology decision.
issue_request: FHIR-7660 is a Published/Persuasive PA DSTU1 issue asking why Encounter.hospitalization.dischargeDiagnosis was only 0..1 and whether additional discharge diagnoses belonged elsewhere, such as Encounter.reason. Its duplicate-family resolution constrained diagnosis-related references and constrained discharge diagnosis to Condition.
initial_application: The discharge-diagnosis part of the issue family was applied by git commit 06c7ab8513, which changed Encounter.hospitalization.dischargeDiagnosis from 0..1 Reference(Any) to 0..* Reference(Condition). Git commit 0983925cea explicitly listed tracker 7660 and the related Encounter diagnosis family while constraining Encounter.indication and adding primaryDiagnosis guidance in the then-current representation.
additional_context: Later final PA decisions replaced the DSTU1 element shape. FHIR-10544 removed hospitalization admitting/discharge diagnosis elements and Encounter diagnosis extensions in favor of Encounter.diagnosis; FHIR-16148 redesigned Encounter.reason and Encounter.diagnosis for R5; FHIR-19285 moved billing diagnosis ranking/type to Account; and FHIR-20484, FHIR-38807, and FHIR-7906 are already represented on the combined branch. FHIR-50827 is a current Triaged terminology issue about Encounter.diagnosis.use and is not final enough to decide here.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current source has Encounter active in fhir.ini, repeatable Encounter.diagnosis, repeatable Encounter.diagnosis.condition limited to CodeableReference(Condition), Encounter.diagnosis.use for diagnosis role/use, and Account.diagnosis sequence/type for billing-related diagnoses. Restoring the retired hospitalization.dischargeDiagnosis element would conflict with later applied decisions.
